items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: At that point, it's still you and Buddy and Richie and Benny Barth. ... Yeah. But our sound was unique.

ctx.x: Because I had seen some jam sessions going down there at times when a band...I remember Count Basie was playing an engagement in Seattle and they came by there and started like a jamming thing. The thing was, people were ready to hear some real music. There was really a big market for it, but there wasn't any groups around there producing it...strong players, a whole group thing...producing it.

There were one or two players here and there, but they were scattered and had their own jobs. And Dave said, 'Well, bring it back and he'd listen to tape or see, whatever. And I went home and I was talking to my brother about it. He just wanted to make some changes. Benny Barth lived, was home, and we were talking about it and said, hey. Buddy was playing vibes now, and I was talking about us...it would be a great sound for a quartet. And Benny said, 'Let's go. I'm ready, man,' because he was...had reached that…
That's when you cooked up the Mastersounds.
